issues.legal_issue: Authorities are not required to accept compensation bonds in payment of agricultural income-tax arrears when the governing payment scheme does not provide for their acceptance.
material_facts: The taxpayer owed agricultural income-tax and a penalty and tendered bonds previously delivered to him as compensation, together with some cash.
The bonds were not yet cashable when tendered.
The applicable provisions provided for recovery of the tax arrears from compensation but did not provide for accepting compensation bonds in payment.
issues.conclusion: The authorities were not required to accept the bonds, and the Collector did not err in refusing them.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(d) of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, as amended, and Rule 8-A provided for recovery of agricultural income-tax arrears from compensation but did not require or authorize acceptance of bonds as payment. Collector of Sultanpur v. Raja Jagdish Prasad Singh established that section 6(d) applied to the relevant tax arrears and that Rule 8-A was mandatory; that did not make bonds an authorized form of tax payment.

predicates.agricultural_tax_recovery_proceeding: The matter concerns recovery of assessed agricultural income-tax arrears.
predicates.bonds_tendered_for_tax: A taxpayer tenders compensation bonds to an authority as payment of tax arrears.
predicates.payment_scheme_silent_on_bond_acceptance: The governing payment scheme does not provide for accepting those bonds as payment of the tax arrears.

issues.definition: When a tax-recovery proceeding involves a tender of bonds and the payment scheme is silent on accepting them, officials may refuse the tender.

issues.legal_issue: Delivery of compensation bonds satisfies the compensation claim even though the bonds have not yet been encashed.
material_facts: The taxpayer had received compensation bonds under the statutory compensation scheme.
The bonds were payable in installments and could not be cashed before their due dates.
The taxpayer argued that compensation remained payable until the bonds were encashed.
issues.conclusion: The compensation claim was satisfied when the bonds were delivered in accordance with the compensation scheme; compensation did not remain payable until encashment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 68 of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, provided for compensation to be paid in cash, bonds, or a combination of both. Rules 62 to 65 governed the bonds' issuance, interest, installments, and payment on presentation. Delivery of bonds in accordance with that scheme constituted payment of compensation.

predicates.compensation_payment_dispute: The dispute concerns whether compensation remains payable after bonds have been issued for it.
predicates.bonds_delivered_as_compensation: The recipient has been delivered bonds as payment of compensation under the applicable compensation scheme.

issues.definition: In a dispute over whether compensation remains payable, delivery of bonds as compensation means the compensation claim is satisfied on delivery.

issues.legal_issue: The negotiability of a bond does not make it legal tender or require a recipient to accept it in payment of a debt.
material_facts: The taxpayer argued that the bonds were negotiable instruments and therefore had to be accepted for payment of tax.
The bonds could be transferred to a person willing to purchase them, but they were not cashable at the time they were tendered.
issues.conclusion: The bonds' negotiability did not make them legal tender or oblige the authorities to accept them in payment of the tax arrears.
issues.legal_principle: A negotiable instrument may be transferred to a willing purchaser, but negotiability alone does not make it legal tender or compel anyone, including the Government, to accept it for a debt.

predicates.payment_tender_dispute: The matter concerns whether a recipient must accept an instrument tendered to pay a debt.
predicates.instrument_is_negotiable: The instrument can be transferred to another person.

issues.definition: In a payment-tender dispute, transferability of an instrument does not require the recipient to accept it.
